pages.title: File:Beachfront B-Roll- Fireworks (Free to Use HD Stock Video Footage).webm

ObjectName.value: Beachfront B-Roll- Fireworks (Free to Use HD Stock Video Footage)

Categories.value: Media from YouTube|Fireworks|Videos of 2013|Uploaded with video2commons|License reviewed by YouTubeReviewBot

ImageDescription.value:
Visit my blog at: http://beachfrontprod.blogspot.com to download the 1920x1080 file in various formats (DNXHD, PhotoJPEG, H.264, WMV and WebM), as well as many more clips, free of charge and free to use.

So it is with great happiness that I am able to share with you these 2 clips, yet I am also greatly disappointed in myself for the state that their audio is in. I was in a great position to visually record these fireworks, but I was also 2 feet away from an air conditioner that was working hard to keep a 5 story building cool. The result was a VERY annoying fan hum throughout the entire show.

I tried to add some audio effects to the footage, but everything I tried seemed to only fit my own personal taste. I DID manage to find a really cool site in the process of trying to find sound for these. It is a site that also offers free media and as far as I'm concerned a place you should visit just as much as you do my blog. It is from the FinalCutKing himself Zach King and it is called http://sweetsoundeffects.com. I have no doubt that with a little TLC, you can personalize the sound for this footage to your liking. Please visit, give him some love, follow him on Facebook and subscribe to him on YouTube.

This footage was shot on the Canon T2i

You are welcome to use them in your projects you are working on or keep them in your clip library for future work. The only thing you cannot do is turn around and offer them AS stock footage. Have fun with them!

Follow Me! Official Site (This is where you download everything!): http://www.beachfrontbroll.com

https://vimeo.com/beachfront

CAPTION: Brubaker Farms is both a diary and green energy producer in Mount Joy, PA on April 19, 2011. The family farm owned by Luke, Mike and Tony Brubaker has approximately 850 cows and 700 young stock, producing 20,200,000 pounds of milk last year. It has 13 full-time employees and more than 1,500 acres of farmland. The digester can handle more than 41,859 metric tons of organic waste, to capture methane that powers a low emission generator producing 225 kW that powers the digester and farm operations. Excess power is sold to the local power grid, allowing the community to benefit from a green energy source. After producing methane, effluent from the digester is pumped into a screw press to squeeze the liquid out for use as fertlizer; and the solid material become the cows’ bedding for Brubaker and other local farms, that is cleaner than sawdust. The bedding saves the farm approximately $30,000 per year. Mount Joy residents can enjoy the fact that the process removes 90% of the odor from the cow manure. The methane itself is odorless and colorless. The system can accept an additional 2,600 gallons of food waste per day from local sources that would otherwise dispose of it in a local landfill. Additionally, their nutrient credits can be sold to the local municipality to help it to meet federal requirements and to keep sewer bills from rising. This provides additional revenue for the farm, and creates environmentally friendly community partnerships. USDA Multimedia by Lance Cheung.

Additional video about organic waste capture and reuse is at https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZWvW594P6n8

ImageDescription.value:
The 2025 iteration of the Wikimania conference held in Nairobi served as a venue for documenting the history of this event over the past two decades. Participants gathered at the Trademark Hotel to discuss the evolution of the conference since its inception in Frankfurt during 2005. Early organizers noted that the initial gathering focused on bringing members of the community together for the first time in a dedicated space. These early events involved logistical challenges such as managing internet connectivity and securing venues within the constraints of limited budgets and volunteer support

Various speakers reflected on the shifting nature of the conference locations and the logistical requirements of hosting attendees. The transition from informal settings such as youth hostels to professional conference facilities mirrored the growth of the Wikimedia movement. Organizers from different years shared personal anecdotes regarding their experiences with site selection and the collaborative efforts required to manage international logistics. The discussion highlighted how the process of selecting host cities changed as the organization matured and adopted more structured planning methods.

Specific editions of the conference were noted for their distinct impact on the broader movement. The 2008 event in Alexandria was cited for its focus on the relationship between libraries and the Wikimedia project. This period saw the development of partnerships between these institutions and the movement. Participants also recalled the technical difficulties and the resourcefulness required to maintain operations in various environments, emphasizing that local community involvement was a factor in the success of these gatherings..

The 2011 event in Haifa was mentioned for its role in the development of Wikidata, which emerged from connections made during that specific conference. Speakers noted that regional collaboration became a recurring theme as the organization looked for ways to support community members across different geographical areas. This period marked a transition in how the foundation interacted with local organizers, with more emphasis placed on long term planning and the inclusion of diverse perspectives from various regions.

Recent editions of the conference incorporated hybrid models to address global accessibility and the constraints imposed by external events. The transition to online formats during the pandemic allowed the movement to maintain engagement while planning for the resumption of in person gatherings. The experience in Singapore and the subsequent regional collaboration models demonstrated the feasibility of hosting events that combined local participation with remote access. This shift enabled broader attendance from regions that previously faced difficulties with international travel..

Looking toward the future, organizers discussed the ongoing efforts to maintain the inclusive nature of the movement. The closing remarks emphasized the importance of volunteers and the role of the conference as a platform for sharing knowledge across different languages and cultures. Reflections on the history of the event served to underline the commitment of participants to the core goals of the Wikimedia movement. The documentation of these two decades provided a context for the continued evolution of the community and the planning of upcoming sessions.

Host: Andrew Lih, Phoebe Ayers
Guests: Organizers of 2005, 2006, 2009, 2011, 2012, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2021, 2023, 2024 editions of Wikimania
